Then Allah the Exalted said: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split.﴾ [al-Qamar 1].

(Iqtarabat) means: has drawn near. But the scholars say that an increase in the form of a word indicates an increase in its meaning. Here, (iqtarabat) has an increase in its form over (qarubat): what is the increase? The hamzah and the taa', which indicates that the drawing near is very near, or that the nearness is very near. So the meaning of (iqtarabat) is: it has drawn very near.

As for as-Sa'ah (the Hour), it is the Day of Resurrection, and Allah the Exalted said concerning it: ﴿So do they await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them unawares? But its signs have already come.﴾ [Muhammad 18], meaning: its signs.

Among its signs is the sending of the Prophet ﷺ, for the sending of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and his being the Seal of the Prophets, is evidence that the Hour has drawn near. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, confirmed this by saying: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he pointed with his middle finger and index finger.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5301) and Muslim (2950/132) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd.]]

Now, the index finger is close to the middle finger, isn't it? There is only a small gap between them, about the size of a fingernail, and this indicates its nearness. But still, how far are we now from the Messenger ﷺ? We are in the fifteenth century after the Hijrah, and that is a long time after the sending of the Messenger ﷺ, yet the world still remains, which indicates that what has passed is very long. Indeed, the Messenger ﷺ once addressed the people at sunset and said: "Indeed, what remains of the world, relative to those who came before you, is only like what remains of this day of yours."[[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (2191) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]]

Therefore: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ means: the Day of Resurrection has drawn near.

﴿And the moon has been split﴾. It seems that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, indicated that this is one of the signs of the Hour. "The moon has been split" means it became two parts, distinct from one another: one part on Mount Abu Qubays and the second on Mount Qu'aiqi'an, meaning one over as-Safa and one over al-Marwah. The distance between as-Safa and al-Marwah, as seen by the eye, is very great, and may take years to cover.

The moon was split in an instant by the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and its parts separated in an instant. This is because the Quraysh used to challenge the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and demand signs from him, and Allah said in reply to them: ﴿Say: The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner. Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book being recited to them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut 50-51]. But it was not sufficient for them, because they were obstinate and did not want the truth. They came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you claim that you are a messenger and that news comes to you from heaven, and such and such; show us a sign." The Prophet ﷺ pointed to the moon and prayed to his Lord, and it split into two halves in an instant. Who can split this great, lofty, horizontal body except the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic! He showed it to them, but did it benefit them? No, it did not benefit them. They said: "Muhammad has bewitched us," and some of them said: "He has bewitched the moon." They denied it, and some of them said to others: "Ask the travelers when they arrive, whether they saw it or not." So they began asking travelers from every direction who came to Makkah, and they said: "Yes, we saw it on such and such night, in such and such way." This applies to those near them, such as the people of the Arabian Peninsula, for example, but those far away may not have seen it. Why? Because of the distance.

As we know now, night here is day in another place, or there are many clouds and fog that prevent seeing it. Therefore, it is never possible for any sensible person to deny the splitting of the moon as a physical splitting, since it is not mentioned in the history of the Greeks, nor in the history of India, nor in such and such. This is not a proof by which what is established in the two Sahihs and others, that the moon truly split in a physical manner, can be refuted.

We believe that the One who is able to fold up the heavens with His right hand as a scroll is folded for writings is able to split the moon into two halves. What thing can overpower Him? Nothing. ﴿Indeed, Allah is never incapable of anything in the heavens or on the earth; indeed He is ever Knowing and Competent.﴾ [Fatir 44].

Therefore there is no basis for the denial of those who deny this from among those who ascribe themselves to Islam and say that the heavenly spheres cannot change. Who created the heavenly spheres? Is it not Allah? Yes. Then He is able to change them: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ [Ya-Sin 82].

So the splitting of the moon is a physical splitting; it split into two halves, and the people saw it and witnessed it. But the arrogant obstinate one accepts nothing.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 2–3:

Therefore He said: ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away﴾ [al-Qamar 2]. "Sign" (āyah) is an indefinite noun in a conditional context, so it means any sign whatsoever: ﴿if they see﴾ means, whatever sign they see, they turn away from it and do not accept it, combining turning away with denial by the tongue.

﴿They turn away﴾ means: with their hearts and their bodies. ﴿And say﴾ with their tongues: ﴿This is continuous magic﴾. You know that magic affects not the essence of things but the seeing of things.

Did you not see that when Moses, peace be upon him, threw down the magicians' ropes and staffs, it appeared to him, from their magic, that they were moving, serpents? The entire valley seemed to be serpents moving about, so much so that Moses sensed fear within himself because of the terror of what he saw. But these ropes and staffs, did they actually turn into serpents, or did they remain as they were? They remained as they were, but according to the viewer's sight they appeared as serpents. So they say: "This is magic; Muhammad has bewitched us, so that our eyes saw the moon as one, while you see it split into two halves."

﴿And say, "It is continuous magic"﴾ [al-Qamar 2]. It was said that the meaning is: passing away, departing, from "marra bi-l-shay'" when one passes beyond a thing; they say, "This is magic that will not last, and has no stability." It was also said: ﴿mustamirr﴾ means that all the signs he brings are magic, i.e., continuous, from "imrār al-shay'" (passing something over) and the persistence of a thing. Whichever meaning is intended, they denied and rejected. Therefore He said: ﴿And they denied﴾, i.e., they denied the Prophet (ﷺ) and denied his signs, ﴿and followed their desires﴾ [al-Qamar 3], i.e., what they wished of falsehood. ﴿And every matter will be settled﴾ [al-Qamar 3], meaning: it must have a final resting place.

As for these deniers, their resting place is humiliation and loss in this world and the Fire in the Hereafter, while the Prophet (ﷺ) and those who followed him, their affair is settled in victory and support in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. May Allah make us and you among its people.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verses 4–5:

﴿And there had already come to them of the news that which contains a deterrent (4), far-reaching wisdom, but warnings avail not﴾ [al-Qamar: 4, 5].

In this sentence Allah, exalted is He, emphasises ﴿And there had already come to them﴾ because they, that is the Quraysh, ﴿there had come to them of the news﴾, meaning the reports in which lay their guidance, their righteousness and their success, ﴿that which contains a deterrent﴾, meaning a deterrent from shirk (associating partners with Allah) and disobedience. Yet they did not benefit from it.

This sentence, as you hear, contains the lam (the emphatic lam) and qad (the particle of emphasis), both of which are particles of emphasis, and it contains an implied oath, indicated by the lam in His words ﴿And there had already come to them﴾. Accordingly, this sentence is emphasised with three emphatics: the oath, the lam, and qad. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is truthful without any emphasis for His report, but this Qur'an is in clear Arabic tongue, and among the eloquence of the Arabic tongue is the emphasis of important matters so that they become fixed and firmly rooted in the mind. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿far-reaching wisdom﴾, meaning that the reports that came to them are wisdom. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾ [an-Nisa: 113]. Wisdom is the fitting of a thing to its proper place, and it is expressed by their saying: placing a thing in its fitting station. There is no doubt that the Shari'ah of Allah is entirely wisdom, all of it conforming to what brings about the welfare of the servants in their livelihood and their hereafter.

His saying ﴿بَالِغَةٌ﴾ (bāligha, far-reaching) means: complete, reaching its intended aim.

﴿فَمَا تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ﴾ (fa-mā tughni al-nudhur, but warnings avail not): the word ﴿مَا﴾ here may be a negation, meaning that the warnings do not avail them anything; and it may be an interrogative in the form of reproach, meaning: then what thing will avail them? Both are correct. The warnings did not avail them anything, and if these warnings containing far-reaching wisdom did not avail them, then what will avail them?!

The answer: nothing, because they are obstinate and arrogant.

So what is the governing element in His saying ﴿The Day they emerge from the graves﴾ [al-Maʿarij 43]? The governing element is His saying ﴿they emerge﴾ (yakhrujūn).

His saying ﴿The Day the Caller calls to a terrible thing﴾ refers to the caller of the Day of Resurrection. ﴿A terrible thing﴾ means a tremendous matter of denial, due to the severity of its terrors, for there is nothing more alien to souls than that Day, since they had never witnessed anything like it.

His saying ﴿with eyes humbled﴾ means their eyes will be lowered and abased, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿They look with a furtive glance﴾ [al-Shura 45]. Thus they will emerge from the graves in this manner, whereas in this world they have a leader, a commander, a guide who knows their path, even if it is a corrupt path.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿Hastening toward the summoner﴾ [al-Qamar 8]. That is, they will be rushing, with necks bowed low. Like a man who hurries and runs: you see him lowering his head. So they will come out of the graves hastening toward the summoner, that is, rushing with their heads lowered, from terror, dread and severity: ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾ [al-Qamar 8]

Reflect on His words ﴿The disbelievers will say﴾, and not "the people will say." As for the believers, it is easy, and all praise is due to Allah. May Allah make us and you among them. ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾

Then God, mighty and majestic, began with the stories of the prophets in this surah in a concise manner, yet it is profoundly impactful. If you read them slowly and reflect upon them, you will find them extremely moving: brief words, yet completely deterring: ﴿The people of Noah denied before them﴾ [al-Qamar 9]. Noah is the first of the messengers. The first messenger that God sent to the inhabitants of the earth was Noah, according to the evidence of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾ [an-Nisa' 163], and He said, exalted is He: ﴿And We had certainly sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their descendants prophethood and scripture﴾ [al-Hadid 26]. Through this we know that what some historians have mentioned, that Idris is the grandfather of Noah, is an undoubted lie, and there was no messenger before Noah. Even in the hadith of intercession there is an explicit statement that he was the first messenger God sent to the inhabitants of the earth. Therefore it is part of our creed that the first of the messengers is Noah, and that the last of the prophets is Muhammad (ﷺ), and he is a prophet and messenger.

﴿The people of Noah denied before them﴾ [al-Qamar 9]. God, mighty and majestic, did not detail this denial, but He sent down a complete surah concerning it, which is Surah Nuh, in which God explained in full detail their denial and their seizing.

﴿So they denied Our servant﴾ [al-Qamar 9], meaning Noah. God described him with servanthood, because servanthood is the most noble of the titles of mankind. Servanthood to God is the most noble of the titles of mankind, and it means humbling oneself to Him in obedience, turning to Him in repentance, relying upon Him, and other such things. Servanthood, considered in itself, is of three types:

The first is general servanthood, which includes all creation, and it is humbling oneself to the universal decree (al-amr al-kawni). An example is the saying of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]. ﴿There is none﴾ means: not everyone in the heavens and the earth is other than in this state, that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. This servanthood is to the universal decree, because the decree of God, mighty and majestic, is universal, and no one can flee from it, however great his strength.

The second type: servanthood specific to the believers, such as the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan 63]. This is general to every believer.

The third: servanthood specific to the prophets. An example is the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿Exalted is He who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra' 1], ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾ [al-Furqan 1], ﴿Praise be to God, who revealed to His servant the Book﴾ [al-Kahf 1]. Among this is this verse: ﴿So they denied Our servant﴾ [al-Qamar 9].

Noah, peace be upon him, remained among them for a thousand years less fifty years, calling them to God. But whenever he called them to God that He might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears so as not to hear his words, covered themselves with their garments so as not to see him, and were arrogant with great arrogance. There is no more eloquent expression of this arrogance than a person putting his hands in his ears so as not to hear the words of the caller, and covering himself with his garment so as to hide from him.

His saying: ﴿And they said, "Madman"﴾ [al-Qamar 9]. The majnun (madman) is one who has lost his reason, who raves about what he does not understand. They said: he is a madman. This accusation was made against all the messengers. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Likewise, no messenger came to those before them but they said, "A sorcerer or a madman"﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 52]. The "or" here is either for variety, meaning some of them say "sorcerer" and some say "madman," or they say both this and that. In any case, Noah was the first to be told that he was a madman.

﴿And he was rebuked﴾ [al-Qamar 9]. Izdijar means he was rebuked with severe rebuke, and zajr is driving away with force and violence. The dal here is converted from a ta'. The scholars have said that an increase in the form indicates an increase in meaning, and the meaning is a severe rebuke. His saying: ﴿And he was rebuked﴾ should not be joined to what precedes it, because if you joined it and said, ﴿And they said, "Madman, and he was rebuked,"﴾ the listener would imagine that they were saying "madman," and that he was rebuked by someone else. But no, the meaning is otherwise: "They denied Our servant and he was rebuked," meaning they denied and rebuked.

Therefore, the better practice is to pause at ﴿And they said, "Madman"﴾, then continue with ﴿And he was rebuked﴾, so that it means these deniers did not limit themselves to denying, but denied, rebuked, threatened, and mocked.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verses 10–11:

When the period grew long, he called upon his Lord: ﴿Indeed, I am overpowered, so help [me]﴾ [al-Qamar 10]. God is greatest! Two words: ﴿Indeed, I am overpowered, so help [me]﴾. He called upon One who is worthy of answering, exalted is He. God responded and said: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth﴾ [al-Qamar 11]. "Fatahna" (We opened), and in another reading: "Fattahna" (We opened, with intensive emphasis), and both are true.

It is appropriate for one who knows the other reading to recite in this way at times and in that way at other times, on condition that this not be done in the presence of the common people; for the common people should not be recited to in a reading that departs from the mushaf in their hands, lest it cause them confusion and perhaps lower the status of the Qur'an in their souls, or they accuse you of error and distortion. But in the presence of students of knowledge and during teaching, or between you and yourself, one should recite the established readings, sometimes with this and sometimes with that.

Just as we say this also regarding the various acts of worship: you do this at one time and that at another, such as the opening supplications (al-istiftahat) and the like.

His saying: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven﴾: ﴿gates﴾ means every gate in the heaven was opened. ﴿With water pouring forth﴾ means poured down in heavy torrents, so it was like the mouths of waterskins, not like the known droplets; no, it was far more intense.

Allah, glorified and exalted, rewards the doers of good with more than their good deeds.

His saying: ﴿And We have left it as a sign, so is there anyone who will take heed?﴾ [Al-Qamar 15]. His saying: ﴿And We have left it﴾, the pronoun "ha" (it) — the commentators differed concerning it. Does the meaning refer to: "And We have left this account, which is the account of Noah and the drowning of his people, as a sign for those who come after them"? This is one view.

The second view: ﴿And We have left it﴾ means the ship, and what is meant is the category (jins) — i.e., the kind of this ship — We left as a sign for those after Noah. Both matters are possible, and the principle in tafsir is that if a verse admits two meanings which do not contradict one another, and neither is more preferable than the other, then it is interpreted according to both meanings together.

So we say: God left the account as a sign and lesson for those who come after Noah, and He left the ship as a sign and lesson, by which those who come after him make its like. What supports this view, and that it is not impossible, is that pronouns sometimes refer to a category rather than to an individual. A parallel is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 12-13]. "We created man from an extract of clay" — what is meant by "man"? Adam. But "Then We placed him as a sperm-drop" — it was not Adam who was placed as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging; rather, "man" here is the category of Adam, namely the children of Adam.

Similarly, according to some scholars, is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps, and made them missiles against the devils﴾ [Al-Mulk 5]. It has also been said that the interrogative is in the sense of a command, and that the meaning is: "So take heed!" Whether we say it is for arousing interest or for command, it is incumbent upon us to remember, and to fear the punishment of Allah, blessed and exalted. Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 16:

﴿Then how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ [al-Qamar: 16]. "Kayfa" (how) here is for emphasis and amazement; that is, "How great were the enemies and the warnings!" It has also been said that the interrogative is for affirmation (taqrir), because Allah makes us acknowledge the punishment and the warnings. But the first meaning is greater: that it is for magnification and exaltation, i.e., "How great was My punishment that descended upon My enemies, and how great were My warnings, which warn and frighten that punishment will descend upon whoever opposes." The punishment that befell the people of Nuh is, with respect to us, considered among the warnings that frighten us from opposing the command of Allah and His Messenger.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 17:

﴿And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [Al-Qamar: 17]. ﴿Yassarna﴾ means: We made it easy (sahhalna).

The Quran is the Book of Allah which was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is called "Quran" because it is recited (yuqra'), i.e., it is recited aloud (yutla).

As for His saying ﴿lidhdhikr﴾ (for remembrance): some of them said: for memorization, and that the Quran is made easy for whoever wishes to memorize it. It was also said: the intended meaning of "dhikr" is remembrance and admonition (al-idkar wa'l-ittiʿaz), meaning that whoever recites the Quran in order to be reminded by it and admonished by it, it becomes easy for him, and he takes heed and benefits. This meaning is closer to the correct view, as evidenced by His saying ﴿fa-hal min muddakir﴾ (so is there any who will remember?), i.e., is there anyone who will remember, although Allah has made the Quran easy for remembrance? Is it not fitting for us, since Allah has made the Quran easy for remembrance, that we should be admonished and remember? Yes.

This is what is fitting: ﴿fa-hal min muddakir﴾.

Verse 18–19 commentary (Ibn 'Uthaymin, Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim)

﴿Ád denied﴾ [al-Qamar: 18]. This is the second nation of those whom God has related to us in this noble surah. 'Ád generally follows the people of Noah, though it may precede them, as in al-Dhariyat. However, the story of Noah is generally the first among the stories of the prophets, because he was the first prophet sent to the people of the earth.

﴿Ád denied﴾: they are the people of Hud, as God the Exalted said: ﴿Oh, away with 'Ád, the people of Hud!﴾ [Hud: 60]. They denied their prophet Hud, peace and blessings be upon him. They were mighty and powerful, and they boasted of their strength and might, saying: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat: 15]. God the Exalted said: ﴿Did they not see that God, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? Yet they used to deny Our signs. So We sent upon them a violent wind﴾ [Fussilat: 15–16].

He says here: ﴿Ád denied, so how was My punishment and My warnings?﴾

The answer is that it was severe and great, falling exactly in its place. The interrogative is therefore for magnification, glorification and affirmation: that God's punishment was great and fell exactly where it was due.

His warnings (nudhur), meaning His signs, were likewise great and fell exactly in their place. So with what did God destroy them? God destroyed them with the most subtle of things: the wind that fills the horizons, yet a person does not sense it, because it is gentle and soft, and a person passes through it easily. The place where we are now is filled with air, is it not? Yet we pass through it without feeling it. It is among the most subtle of things.

God destroyed 'Ád, who boasted of their strength, with this wind, as God the Mighty and Majestic said here: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a violent wind on a day of continuous ill omen﴾ [al-Qamar: 19]. The sentence here is emphasized with (inna), and ﴿We sent﴾ means the Lord Himself, the Mighty and Majestic; that is, the Lord refers to Himself by saying ﴿We sent﴾, and the pronoun is in the plural for magnification.

﴿Upon them﴾, i.e., upon 'Ád. ﴿A violent wind﴾, i.e., one with a roaring sound, because of its strength and force, such that its mere passage is heard as a roar, even if it does not strike anything that would produce a roar, because it is very strong and great. It was the western wind: it came from the west, i.e., from the direction of the west, upon 'Ád. They said: ﴿This is a cloud bringing us rain﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 24], for they had suffered drought for years before that. When it approached with its blackness, its greatness and its roaring, they said: ﴿This is a cloud bringing us rain.﴾ But the matter was the opposite: it was a wind containing painful punishment, a barren wind, with no rain in it and no hope that rain would come from it.

Here God the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a violent wind﴾, i.e., what kind of wind? The western one, which comes from the direction of the west.

﴿Violent﴾, i.e., intense in sound and roaring because of its strength and speed.

﴿On a day of continuous ill omen﴾: ﴿ill omen﴾ means a day of misfortune, ﴿continuous﴾ with respect to 'Ád. It was not so at all times; the day on which they were destroyed was not itself a continuous ill omen in itself, but for these people it was a day of continuous ill omen, as God the Exalted said about the people of Noah: ﴿They were drowned and then made to enter a fire﴾ [Nuh: 25]. These people were destroyed by the wind and then made to enter the fire. So the ill omen (nahs), i.e., misfortune, remained continuous for them; the punishment of the Hereafter is joined to the punishment of this world.

﴿Snatching up people﴾ [al-Qamar: 20], i.e., seizing them with severity and force and lifting them up into the sky—we ask Allah for well-being—to the point that some of them said: it lifts them until a person disappears from sight because of its height, then casts him down to the earth. When they fall to the earth, they fall on the top of their heads, and then the head is separated from the body because of the violence of the impact.

﴿Snatching up people, as if they were﴾ while falling to the earth, ﴿trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾. A'jaz means the bases (usul), and the palm tree is well known; al-munqa'ir means that which has fallen from its root. The meaning is: as if they were palm trees that had fallen from their roots and only their trunks remained. Why did they become like palm trunks? Because they had no heads, according to what the exegetes said, since their heads were separated from them because of the violence of the impact. Glory be to the Strong, the Mighty! These people, who were strong and powerful, came to this state by a wind from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Snatching up people as if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees (20). Then how was My punishment and My warning﴾ [al-Qamar: 20–21]. Here I ask: here He says ﴿as if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾, and in al-Haqqah: ﴿as if they were trunks of hollow palm trees﴾ [al-Haqqah: 7]. The meaning is close, but it is part of the eloquence of the Qur'an that the speech proceeds in a single pattern. There, ﴿hollow﴾ (khawiyah) suits the closing rhymes (fawasil) in al-Haqqah, does it not? Here, ﴿uprooted﴾ (munqa'ir) suits the closing rhymes in Surat al-Qamar, because the harmony and consistency of the speech is part of the perfection of its eloquence.

﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 22] Allah the Exalted repeated this at the end of each story so that we would be eager to remember the Qur'an, to ponder the Qur'an, and to understand the Qur'an, since it is made easy. The sentence, as you can see, is emphasized by three emphatics: the oath (al-qasam), the lam, and (qad), which indicates desire, or rather encouragement, to remember the Qur'an and be mindful of it through remembrance ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾.

We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make us and you among those who take heed from the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; indeed He is capable of all things.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 23–24:

﴿Thamūd denied the warnings﴾ [al-Qamar: 23]. That is, they denied the warnings that came to them, which were the signs brought by Ṣāliḥ, peace be upon him. Their dwellings are known today in the land of al-Ḥijr, on the road to Tabūk from Madinah. Ṣāliḥ, peace be upon him, was sent to his people calling them to worship Allah alone, without partner, like all the prophets. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiyā': 25], and He the Exalted said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghūt (false deities)." So among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was decreed﴾ [al-Naḥl: 36]. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him to his people and gave him a sign, which was a she-camel that had a share of water, and they had a share of water. That is, the great well of the camel, abundant in water, was one day for the camel to come and drink. It is mentioned that when she drank a vessel of water, the one who gave her to drink would milk from her an amount of milk equal to what she had drunk. This is one of the signs of Allah Mighty and Majestic: a she-camel drinks water and then immediately produces milk. This is not a customary thing, but it is a sign from the signs of Allah Mighty and Majestic, which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, showed them so that they might take heed. Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 25:

﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ [al-Qamar: 25] This is also a rhetorical question of contempt. It means: how can the Reminder be sent down upon him from among us? What has distinguished him? All of this is mere doubts, not proofs. His being a human does not prevent him from being a messenger; rather, the messenger to mankind must necessarily be a human, because Allah says: ﴿And they say, "Why has an angel not been sent down to him?" And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided; then they would not be reprieved. (8) And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man and would have covered for them what they cover.﴾ [al-An'am: 8, 9] That is, if We sent an angel, it would necessarily be in the form of a man, so that he could mix with people and become familiar with them; and if We made the angel a man, We would confuse them with what they already confuse themselves with, and the matter would become muddled.

So let us now consider: the first doubt is that they said he is a human; the second, that he is one of us, not distinguished over us in anything; the third, that he is a single individual who has not been supported; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And present to them the parable of the people of the town, when the messengers came to it. (13) When We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We strengthened [them] with a third﴾ [Ya-Sin: 13, 14], meaning We reinforced them. These people say: one is not enough; he must be reinforced by a second and a third.

The fourth: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ [al-Qamar: 25], meaning: how can the Reminder and the revelation be sent down upon him from among us? This is impossible.

So: these are four doubts, which they regard as proofs requiring the rejection of Salih, peace be upon him. In reality they are not proofs; they are mere confusion and misguidance. Thus are the falsifiers, my brothers: in every age and place, the falsifiers raise doubts against the truth. But Allah, glorified and exalted, must make the truth clear, so that whoever is destroyed is destroyed after a clear proof, and whoever lives lives after a clear proof.

Then they said: ﴿Rather, he is an arrogant liar﴾ [al-Qamar: 25]. ﴿Rather﴾ here serves to refute their claim that he is true. ﴿Liar﴾ is an intensive form, and at the same time a descriptive; because the pattern fa''al comes for emphasis and also for description. When you say "so-and-so is a carpenter," it means he is one of the carpenters; otherwise he would only have carpentered once. And when you say "so-and-so is a blacksmith," because of his frequent use of iron, it becomes an intensive. They regard him, may Allah protect us, as a liar characterized by lying, having no attribute except lying, and one who lies much. ﴿Arrogant﴾ means: insolent, haughty, self-magnifying, proud, claiming what is not his.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verses 26–27:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They will know tomorrow who is the liar, the insolent one.﴾ [al-Qamar 26] "They will know tomorrow." When? On the Day of Resurrection. The *sin* here is for *tahqiq* (affirmation, confirming that something will certainly happen) and *taqrib* (indicating nearness), because when you say "Zayd will stand up" (*sayaqum Zayd*), this is also an affirmation and an indication of nearness.

If someone asks: affirmation is well known, since it is the truth that the Hour is coming, with no doubt about it, but how is there nearness?

We say: Allah says: ﴿And what would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ [al-Ahzab 63] and ﴿And what would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ [al-Shura 17]. And among the well-known proverbs: everything that is coming is near.

The one who has a thousand years remaining is nearer than the one who has only ten minutes past, is he not? Because what has passed for ten minutes cannot be returned, but the future must come: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is coming.﴾ [al-An'am 134]

So, ﴿they will know﴾: the *sin* here is for what?

* Students: For *tahqiq*.

* Shaykh: And what else?

* Students: *Taqrib*.

* Shaykh: And *taqrib*: ﴿They will know tomorrow who is the liar, the insolent one.﴾ "Tomorrow" is the Day of Resurrection. It is called "tomorrow" because it comes after your day. "They will know who is the liar, the insolent one." So who is it, now? Let me ask you: is it Salih or Thamud?

* Student: Salih.

* Shaykh: Salih?

* Student: The second.

* Shaykh: The second. Thamud. They will know on the Day of Resurrection who the liar, the insolent one is. Is Salih the liar and insolent one, or are they? This is a great warning: ﴿And those who wronged will know what return they will be returned to.﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 227]. Man is a human being who is heedless of this great Day. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, their hearts are in confusion about this.﴾ [al-Mu'minun 63], meaning: about the deeds of the Hereafter. "Rather, their hearts are in confusion," covered over regarding the deeds of the Hereafter: ﴿And they have deeds other than that which they are doing.﴾ [al-Mu'minun 63], meaning: the deeds of this world, which they are doing. He used a nominal sentence, meaning that they are certain in performing these deeds, they do not abandon them and they are not negligent about them, whereas regarding the Hereafter they are heedless of it.

﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them﴾ [al-Qamar 27]. "Indeed, We" refers to Himself, the Majestic and Exalted, and He used the plural form to magnify Himself, the Majestic and Exalted, because of the greatness of His attributes, the abundance of His perfections and the abundance of His hosts. Therefore He refers to Himself with the form of magnification: ﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them.﴾ Meaning: sending it forth. ﴿As a trial for them﴾ as a test: will they believe or not believe? And what was the outcome? Did they believe or not? They did not believe.

In this there is an indication that Allah the Exalted may show a person signs of the kind that would make human beings believe, yet if he becomes arrogant, his arrogance is arrogance with knowledge, so his punishment is more severe and more painful. For this reason Allah made the she-camel a trial, because it showed them the truth, but they did not accept it. Be attentive to this gradual leading by Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, be attentive. If Allah makes the means of sin easy for you, do not commit it, for Allah may make the means of sin easy for a person as a trial for him. Have you considered the People of the Sabbath among the Children of Israel? The means of sin were made easy for them as a trial. Allah had forbidden them to hunt fish on the Sabbath, so the fish would come on the Sabbath, floating on the surface of the water and in great abundance. But they were committed and did not hunt fish on the Sabbath. Then, when the period became long for them, they were unable to master themselves, so they returned to their nature, which is treachery, trickery and deceit. They devised a stratagem to catch fish: they would set up nets on Friday, so the fish would enter the nets, and on Sunday they would take the fish. This is an obvious trick, so Allah transformed them into apes. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And you have already known those among you who transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath, so We said to them, "Be apes, despised and driven away."﴾ [al-Baqarah 65]

In the early period of this Ummah, Allah forbade the hunting of game to those in the state of ihram: ﴿Do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 95]. So Allah sent game to them while they were in ihram, within reach of their hands and their spears. That means that the one crawling could be caught by hand, such as a rabbit for example, or a gazelle that one person could catch with his hand. ﴿And your spears﴾ [al-Ma'idah 94] means birds. Birds could only be reached with an arrow, because they were far away, but the bird would fly as if it were on the ground, and the spear would reach it. A trial. Here, did Allah make the means of sin easy for them or not?

* Students: He made them easy.

* Shaykh: He made them easy. But the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, the best of people, none of them took a single game animal, may Allah be pleased with them, whereas the Children of Israel devised stratagems and deceived Allah. As for the predecessors of this Ummah, may Allah grant us and you success in accompanying them in their deeds in this world and in their dwellings in the Hereafter, they did not take any.

So here, Allah sent the she-camel as a trial for Thamud, but it did not benefit them.

That means Allah said to their messenger Salih: wait for these people and be patient; be patient, for victory is near.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 29:

So they asked him to slaughter her, and we ask Allah for well-being. Was this companion, the strong and courageous one whom they regarded as more daring than themselves, regardless of his name (some exegetes named him, but that does not matter), reluctant? No, he did not hesitate or delay, but hastened forward.

﴿So he took hold (of the camel) and hamstrung her﴾ [al-Qamar 29]. Ta'ataa (تعاطى) is of the form tafā'ala, from al-'atā' (العطاء), meaning: he gave himself over (to the task) and quickly. The fa' (ف) in His words ﴿fa-ta'ataa﴾ indicates speed: from the moment they called him, without delay, he immediately ﴿hamstrung﴾ the she-camel, and we ask Allah for well-being. He first cut her limbs, then slaughtered her, and she was one of the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and one of their benefits. But, and we ask Allah for well-being, their souls did not accept ﴿so he took hold and hamstrung her﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 30:

﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ [al-Qamar: 30] Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says, addressing mankind: ﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ Did it fall in its proper place? And was it severe?

The answer: Yes, it fell in its proper place, and it was severe. What a punishment this was!

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 31:

﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a single blast⁠﴾ [al-Qamar: 31] They were struck with a cry—we seek refuge in Allah—together with the quake. In the sky there were sounds, and in the earth there were tremors. The quake and the cry drove them out, ﴿so they became, in their homes, prostrate corpses, as if they had never flourished therein⁠﴾ [Hud: 67–68]. It is as if they had never existed.

﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a single blast, so they became like the dry crushed remains of a fence builder's enclosure⁠﴾ [al-Qamar: 31].

That is: the hazar (enclosure) that a person makes for his sheep. I do not know whether you are familiar with this or not. The Bedouin in the desert makes an enclosure for the sheep out of dry wood, palm fronds, and the like, so that they do not escape and so that predators do not attack them. This enclosure, with the passage of time and the sun and the winds, crumbles until it disappears. These mighty, powerful people who denied their Messenger became like the crushed remains (hashim) of the enclosure, that is, like a fence when it is destroyed. This is one of the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the completeness of His power and dominion: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is⁠﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82], so they became like the crushed remains of the enclosure.

And indeed, We have made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember? [al-Qamar: 32]. "And indeed, We have made the Qur'an easy for remembrance" has already been explained, and we said that the meaning is that Allah, the Exalted, made the Qur'an easy: He made its meanings easy for whoever reflects upon it, and He made its words easy for whoever memorizes it. So when you turn to the Qur'an sincerely for memorization, Allah makes it easy for you, and when you turn to it truly for reflection and understanding of its meanings, Allah makes it easy for you. "And indeed, We have made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember?" Here "hal" (هل, "is there") is for stimulating interest: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, urges us to take heed of the Qur'an so that we may be admonished by it. May Allah make us and you among those who recite it in its truest recitation, in words, meaning and action. Indeed, He is over all things Competent.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 33–34:

We have reached the words of Allah, may He be exalted, in Surat al-Qamar: ﴿The people of Lut denied the warners.﴾ [al-Qamar 33] The people of Lut were folk who disbelieved in Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, and associated partners with Him. What distinguished them among their sins was this foul and monstrous act, which is sodomy (liwat), meaning the coming of males to males. Their prophet warned them against this and said to them: ﴿Do you approach the males among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a people transgressing.﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 165-166].

But they, Allah forbid, persisted in this until the punishment came upon them. In this surah, Allah, may He be exalted, mentioned the stories of the prophets in summary form, as has already been discussed, and here He said: ﴿The people of Lut denied the warners.﴾ "Nudhur" is the plural of "nadhir" (warner), and refers to the admonitions with which Lut, peace be upon him, warned them. The use of the plural indicates that he repeated this to them, but they refused and insisted upon this act. Allah then explained their punishment in His words: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a violent wind, except the family of Lut; We saved them at dawn.﴾ [al-Qamar 34]. "Hasiban" means something that pelts them from the sky. Allah rained upon them stones of sijjil, and their houses were destroyed until their upper part became their lower part, because when a building collapses, its top becomes its bottom.

﴿Except the family of Lut﴾: the family of Lut are his household, except his wife, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So We brought out whoever was in it of the believers. But We found not in it except one house of Muslims.﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 35-36]. A prophet who is sent to his people and none follows him except his household, and even his wife, who was a disbeliever, yet he remained patient until he was permitted to leave.

﴿We saved them at dawn﴾, meaning: in the pre-dawn hour, in the morning. This is because the punishment seized these people in the morning, just as the punishment of 'Ad began in the morning: ﴿seven nights and eight days, continuously﴾ [al-Haqqah 7], since it began in the morning. So the punishment seized them, Allah forbid, in the morning, and Allah destroyed them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 35:

﴿As a favour from Us﴾ [al-Qamar: 35]. That is: We bestowed a favour upon the family of Lut from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in two respects.

The first respect: Allah saved them.

The second respect: Allah destroyed their enemy.

Because destroying the enemy is among the favours of Allah. Thus the favour of Allah upon the family of Lut was in their deliverance and in the destruction of their enemy.

﴿Thus do We reward those who give thanks﴾ [al-Qamar: 35]. That is: like this recompense, which is deliverance and favour, We reward those who give thanks for the favour of Allah. And giving thanks for the favour of Allah, Most High, O brothers, is to carry out His obedience, and it is not merely a person's saying, "I thank Allah." Rather, it is necessary to carry out obedience.

For this reason, whoever says, "I thank Allah" while persisting in His disobedience is not a thankful person. Rather, he is ungrateful for the favour and mocks Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, since the requirement of a favour is that Allah be thanked, but he has done the opposite. Allah, Most High, said: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin? (28) Hell, which they will enter, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [Ibrahim: 28-29]. So everyone who thanks Allah, Allah, Most High, will deliver him and destroy his enemy.

And indeed he had warned them of Our assault, but they disputed the warnings. (Qur'an 54:36)

Meaning: Lut (peace be upon him) warned his people of the seizing (al-batshah), which is taking by force. "But they disputed the warnings" means: they doubted it and did not believe in it.

And indeed they sought to make him (Lot) forfeit his guests. (Qur'an 54:37)

This means that his people sought to take his guests, who had come to him from the angels. Allah the Exalted had sent the angels to him in the form of beardless young men of beauty and comely appearance, as a trial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When the people of Lot heard of these guests, they came hastening toward him (يُهرَعون), rushing, intending these guests in order to commit the abomination with them, and Allah forbid. So they sought to take his guests, and Allah obliterated their eyes.

As for how He obliterated their eyes, whether Jibril struck them with his wing or otherwise, Allah knows best. What is incumbent upon us is to believe that Allah the Exalted obliterated their eyes until they could no longer see.

"So taste My punishment and warnings" (Qur'an 54:37)

The command here is one of humiliation, or it is a command of decree (amr kawni), meaning that Allah commanded them with a command of humiliation, or a decreed command that they taste the punishment. A similar statement is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted, about the one in the Hellfire: "Taste it! Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble" (Qur'an 44:49). This command is without doubt a command of humiliation, not a command of honour or of permission.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 38–40:

﴿And certainly an abiding punishment came upon them early in the morning (38). So taste My punishment and warnings﴾ [al-Qamar: 38, 39]. He means that the punishment came upon them in the morning, while they had just risen from sleep and were facing their day in joy, each one of them thinking about what he would do that day. Then suddenly the punishment fell upon them—we ask Allah for well-being. ﴿So taste My punishment and warnings (39). And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾.

Among the lessons in this verse: those whose nature and disposition Allah had corrupted, Allah overturned their buildings upon them by pelting them with stones of sijjil, so the buildings collapsed until their top became their bottom. It has also been said that Allah, exalted is He, overturned their dwellings with them—uprooting them from their foundations, lifting them up and then flipping them over. If this is sound, then Allah is over all things competent; and if it is not sound, then we are only obliged to adhere to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an: that they were rained upon with stones of sijjil, so the building collapsed on them.

From this, the scholars have derived that the one who commits sodomy (liwat) is to be killed in every case, both the active partner and the passive partner. This is the preponderant view: that sodomy requires the death penalty in every case, and it is not like fornication (zina), where a distinction is made between a married person and an unmarried one. As for sodomy, the one who commits it is killed in every case, so long as both the active and passive partners are adult and sane; both must be killed in every case, except the one who was coerced—the coerced person bears no liability.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, unanimously agreed on killing the active and passive partners, but they differed on how they should be killed. Some of them said: they are killed by stoning with stones until they die. Others said: they are killed by being thrown from the highest place in the town and then stones are thrown after them. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, burned the practitioners of sodomy with fire, and likewise Khalid ibn al-Walid and one of the caliphs of the Umayyads burned them with fire, owing to the enormity of their crime—we seek refuge in Allah. Moreover, when this sin spreads among a people, their men become like women, and one of them goes after the virile men until they commit the sin with him—we seek refuge in Allah. The circumstances are overturned, and offspring are lost; that is, people turn toward males and leave aside women, who are the tilth of men. Guarding against it is difficult, for one cannot find two people and say: how did you keep company with this one, for example? But if we find a man and a woman, one can guard against them. Therefore the remedy for society against this ugly and abominable act is that the active and passive partners be killed. Concerning this there is a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lut, kill the active and the passive partner."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4462) and al-Tirmidhi (1456) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

Therefore, brothers, it is obligatory upon us to guard against this to the utmost degree, and to keep watch over our children: where have they gone? From where have they come? Who are their friends? Are they upright or not? So that we may protect society from this wicked deed.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 40]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made the Qur'an easy for remembrance—for memorizing it and for understanding its meaning. This statement is intended to encourage memorizing the Qur'an and reflecting upon its meaning, because it is facilitated and easy. Try to reflect upon the verses of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in order to understand their meaning, and see how Allah makes their understanding easy for you, so that you grasp from them what many people do not grasp. This is why He said: ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 40]. The interrogative here is for stimulating interest; that is: Is there anyone who will remember, who will take heed and be admonished by what is in the Qur'an?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 41–42:

﴿And there had certainly come to the family of Pharaoh the warnings.﴾ He means his people, headed by Pharaoh, as Allah the Exalted related in many other verses that He sent Musa to Pharaoh and his chiefs.

"The warnings had come to them." As for an-nudhur (النُّذُر), it has been said that it means al-indhar (الإنذار), which is intimidation, and it has been said that it is the plural of nadhir (نذير), meaning everything by which the servant is warned. What is meant by it is the signs that Musa brought, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa nine clear signs﴾ [al-Isra 101]. This latter view is the correct one: that an-nudhur is the plural of nadhir and not in the sense of al-indhar. This is supported by His saying: ﴿They denied Our signs, all of them﴾ [al-Qamar 42], i.e., they denied all the signs that indicate the truthfulness of Musa's message, peace be upon him and his family, and they denied them and said: Musa is a madman and he is a sorcerer, to the extent that Pharaoh, out of his arrogance, said: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is a madman﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 27].

When they denied the signs, Allah seized them ﴿with the seizing of One Mighty, Omnipotent﴾ [al-Qamar 42], the Majestic and Exalted. ﴿Mighty﴾ means Overpowering, and ﴿Omnipotent﴾ means Capable. Yet the word (muqtadir) is more emphatic than (qadir), because of the additional letters it contains; it has been said that an increase in the form indicates an increase in meaning, though this is generally so and not always.

Allah mentioned that His seizing of them was a seizing by One Mighty and Omnipotent because Pharaoh was arrogant, and used to say: ﴿I am your lord, the Most High﴾ [an-Nazi'at 24], and used to mock Musa and the one who sent him. So it was fitting that Allah mention His seizing them as the seizing of One Mighty and Omnipotent, who is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Allah has summarized this story in this verse, but He explained it in many verses. Their seizing was by drowning them in the sea. Allah drowned him by the same thing he had boasted of, for he used to say to his people: ﴿O my people, does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flowing beneath me?﴾ He was asserting this to them, and they would say: Yes. ﴿Will you not then see? (51) Or am I better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly express himself?﴾ [az-Zukhruf 51–52], meaning by that Musa. Allah drowned them in the sea when Pharaoh gathered his troops and pursued Musa and those who followed him, intending to destroy them. But Allah, by His praise and His might, destroyed him.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 48:

﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces﴾ [al-Qamar: 48] They are dragged with the kind of dragging by which a carcass is pulled away from the dwellings, and they are not dragged on their backs but upon their faces, we seek refuge with Allah. It is said: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾ [al-Qamar: 48]. Allah the Exalted has said in another verse: ﴿Is one who shields with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is safe]?﴾ [al-Zumar: 24]. ﴿Shields with his face﴾: he who in this world used to shield himself from the heat with his hands, to protect his face. But in the Fire he has nothing that can shield his face from the Fire; rather he shields with his face, we ask Allah for well-being, meaning he has no shield that protects his face from the heat of the Fire. So they are dragged in the Fire upon their faces.

This, my brothers, is not "the fables of the ancients," nor are they stories that are told. This is a truth we bear witness to, by Allah, as if we were seeing it with our own eyes. It must be that this applies to every criminal: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces﴾. And those who drag them are the angels appointed over them, for the Fire has angels appointed over it. It is said: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾.

Consider, my brother, the humiliation: of the body and of the heart. The bodily humiliation is that they are dragged upon their faces; the humiliation of the heart is that they are rebuked. It is said: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾, meaning: burn in it. Saqar is one of the names of the Fire. We ask Allah for well-being for us and for you.

Then He, may His majesty be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created with predestination﴾ [al-Qamar 49]. When He mentioned the punishment of the people of the Fire, and then was going to mention the bliss of the people of Paradise, He mentioned between them that this creation and its variation is by the predestination (qadar) of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So every created thing is by qadar. Pay attention, my brother: every grain of sand in a dune is created by qadar, every drop that falls on the earth from the cloud is created by qadar. ﴿All things﴾ encompasses everything other than the Creator, because there is nothing but the created and the Creator. If everything is created, then the Creator alone is the First, before whom there is nothing, and the Last, after whom there is nothing, and the Manifest, above whom there is nothing, and the Hidden, beneath whom there is nothing.

The Prophet ﷺ said: «Everything is by qadar, even incapacity and astuteness»[[Narrated by Muslim (2655/18) from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar.]]. Al-ʿajz (incapacity): meaning a person's laziness; al-kays (astuteness): meaning a person's resolve and energy in seeking what benefits him and keeping away from what harms him. Everything.

This noble verse is evidence that man is created by Allah, the Exalted, and that his actions are created by Allah, and that everything has been decreed and concluded. If that is so, to whom does a person turn when adversity touches him? To Allah, the Creator. And when he desires ease, he also turns to Allah, the Creator. He should not boast or become conceited with himself when he obtains what he sought, nor despair when a calamity befalls him, for the matter is in the hand of Allah.

For this reason the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: «The strong believer is better than the weak believer»[[Narrated by Muslim (2664/34) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. The strong is strong in his faith, strong in his will, his resolve and his energy, and it is not meant as strong in body. Physical strength is either for you or against you: if you use it in righteous deeds, it is for you; and if you are unable to do them while you were doing them in a state of strength, it is recorded for you; and if you use this strength in disobedience to Allah, it is against you. But what is meant by his saying, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, «the strong» is in his faith and his will; as for physical strength, it is for you or against you.

He said: «and in each there is good». In each of the strong and the weak there is good. Scholars of rhetoric call this sentence a precautionary clause (jumla ihtirāziyya), because when he said «the strong believer is better than the weak believer», one might suppose that the weak believer has no good in him, so he said «and in each there is good». There are parallels to this, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the victory and fought﴾, meaning before the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, ﴿and fought. Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought. But to each Allah has promised the best﴾ [al-Hadid 10]: each of these and those. The meaning is: do not think that this disparity diminishes the standing of the others or deprives them of good. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home] other than those with a disability and those who strive in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred the strugglers with their wealth and lives over those who sit [at home] by a degree. But to each Allah has promised the best﴾ [an-Nisa 95].

Here the Prophet ﷺ said: «The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and in each there is good. Be eager for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not become incapable». So when you do that, you are eager for what benefits and you seek help from Allah, and you are resolute, energetic and strong in your aim. He said: «If something befalls you, do not say: "If only I had done such-and-such, it would have been such-and-such." Rather say: "This is the qadar of Allah, and whatever He wills, He does," for "if only" opens the work of Satan». It is incumbent upon you to strive for good; it is not incumbent upon you that everything you want be accomplished for you.

The essential point is that everything is by qadar, even incapacity and astuteness. Whoever Allah has decreed guidance for, it is by qadar; and whoever He has decreed wretchedness for, it is also by qadar. But what is the cause of Allah's decreeing wretchedness for the servant? It is the very deed itself, according to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾ [as-Saff 5].

He said: "And Our command is but one [act], like a glance of the eye" (Surah al-Qamar 54:50). That is: Our command regarding what We wish to come into being is but one, i.e., one time only, without repetition, "like a glance of the eye" [al-Qamar 50], without any delay. Glory be to Allah! The command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is one; there is no repetition. And the second [act] is with immediate speed, as swift as can be, like a glance of the eye: "Be, and it is" (kun fayakun).

It is widespread among the common people that they say: "O You whose command is between the Kaf and the Nun" (ya man amruhu bayn al-kaf wa al-nun). This is a mistake. The command of Allah is not between the Kaf and the Nun, but after the Kaf and the Nun, because Allah said: "Be, and it is." When? After "Be." So their saying "between the Kaf and the Nun" is an error. That is, the matter is not completed between the Kaf and the Nun; the matter is not completed except by the Kaf and the Nun, but it is after the Kaf and the Nun immediately, like a glance of the eye. And if you wish to see the wonders of this, look at earthquakes striking hundreds of villages, or thousands of villages, and in a single moment you see them destroyed in one moment. Even if bulldozers, bulldozers [draglines] and bombs came, they would not do what one moment of the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does. Ask the experts on earthquakes and you will find the answer.

Look at what is greater than that: the dead in their graves, the insects, the animals, and all things will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with one word, as Allah, the Exalted, said: "It will be but one shout, and at once they will all be brought before Us" (Ya-Sin 36:53). I ask Allah to make me and you among those who are brought forward to good, [a single] "shout" only, "and at once they will all" — all of them — "before Us" — i.e., with Us — "brought forward." Thus Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, fulfilled His promise. "And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye": like the blink of an eye.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And We have certainly destroyed your likes, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar 51]. The address is to the disbelievers of Quraysh. His words ﴿ashyā'akum﴾ (your likes) mean: those who resemble you among the earlier disbelievers. In this surah Allah, the Exalted, has related to us from their news what contains a lesson and an admonition. He related to us what happened to the people of Nuh (Noah), what happened to 'Ad, Thamud, and Lut (Lot), and the family of Fir'awn (Pharaoh). In this there is a reminder for whoever wishes to be reminded. For this reason He said: ﴿so is there any who will remember?﴾, meaning: is there anyone who takes heed and draws a lesson from what befell the earlier peoples, that the same should befall the later ones? For Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has no favoritism or kinship between Himself and His servants. Rather, the most honored of them in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of them toward Him, regardless of what race they are, in what place they are, or in what time they are. As Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat 13].

Then He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And everything they have done is in the Zubur﴾ [Al-Qamar 52]. ﴿Kull﴾ (kull, "every/all") is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿fi al-zubur﴾ (fi al-zubur, "in the scriptures") is its predicate (khabar). This is not an instance of ishtighal (ishtighal, the construction in which a verb is suspended over a pronoun referring to its object), but a pure predicate. That is, ﴿kull﴾ cannot be the object of ﴿fa'aluhu﴾ (fa'aluhu, "they did it"); rather it is the subject in every case, and ﴿fi al-zubur﴾ is the predicate. ﴿Everything they have done﴾ means that whatever the earlier nations or the later nations did, it is written ﴿in the zubur﴾, that is, in the books. The recording of deeds is of two kinds: a prior recording and a subsequent recording. The prior recording is a recording that this will do such-and-such; no reward or punishment follows from this recording, because the person has not yet been held accountable for it. The subsequent recording is the recording that he did it: when a person does a good deed, God records it; when he does an evil deed, God records it. It is this subsequent recording that carries reward and punishment.

By what we have established, the difficulty that some people have with the saying of God, blessed and exalted, ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those of you who strive and those who are steadfast﴾ [Muhammad 31], is removed. Some people find this verse problematic: how can He say ﴿until We know﴾ when He already knows? It is said that ﴿until We know﴾ means the knowledge that results in reward; as for God's prior knowledge, no reward or punishment results from it.

So ﴿everything they have done is in the Zubur﴾ means that everything they did is written. The prior recording is the recording of what he will do now, written in advance, and the subsequent recording is the recording that he did it. Which recording carries reward or punishment, the prior or the subsequent? The subsequent. As for the prior recording, God, glorified and exalted, wrote everything in the Preserved Tablet, as in the authentic hadith: "When God created the Pen, He said to it: Write. It said: My Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write what will be until the Day of Resurrection" [Abu Dawud (4700) and al-Tirmidhi (2155), from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit].

Thus, in that moment, what is to be until the Day of Resurrection was decreed. What afflicted a person would not have missed him, and what missed him would not have afflicted him. We believe in this. God, exalted, said: ﴿Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a Book. Indeed, that is easy for God﴾ [Al-Hajj 70]. He, mighty and majestic, also said: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 105]. The subsequent recording is that when a person does a deed, God records it. God, exalted, said: ﴿No! Rather, you deny the Recompense. But indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [Al-Infitar 9–11]. This recording is the one that carries reward and punishment.

﴿And everything they have done is in the Zubur﴾: the meaning of the verse is that everything a person does is recorded, every single thing. So do not think that anything of yours will ever be lost. As God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say: "Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present﴾. Glory be to God! After hundreds of years known only to God, they will find it present. ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [Al-Kahf 49].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 54, verse 53:

﴿And every small and great thing is inscribed﴾ [al-Qamar: 53]. Every small thing among what occurs in this universe, whether creatures, their attributes, or their actions, is inscribed, that is, written down in the Mighty Book, the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Every small and great thing, even the thorn that a person is pricked by, is written down, and even whatever weighs the mass of an atom's weight of deeds is written down. Every small and great thing: if you believe in this, my brother, and you must believe in it, then you must beware of disobedience. Beware of disobeying with your speech, your action, or your omission. Beware of disobeying, because everything is written. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer ready [to record]﴾ [Qaf: 18]. The same applies to what one does. For if words are written down, and they are thousands of times more numerous than actions, how many letters do you utter that cannot be contained? How many actions do you perform? Fewer, though they cannot be counted, but they are few in comparison with speech. So if speech is written down, actions are written down all the more so.

You must fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; fear your Lord and do not disobey Allah. When you hear Allah say something as a report, say: "I believe in it and I affirm it." When you hear Allah say something as a command, say: "I believe in it, and I hear and obey." When you hear Him forbid something, say: "I believe in it, and I hear and obey." Then abandon what is forbidden and perform what is commanded. This is advice.

﴿And every small and great thing is inscribed﴾. The movements are recorded; the letters, the letters of speech, are recorded. Everything is recorded.

This is a continuation of Qur'an 54:54–55: **"Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers."** It is set against His words: **"Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness, the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces"** (54:47–48).

**"Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers."** The word *jannat* (gardens) is the plural of *jannah*. Allah the Exalted mentioned its categories in Surat al-Rahman (Surah al-Rahman), four of them: **"And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens"** (55:46), then He said: **"And besides them are two gardens"** (55:62). So they are four. The four Allah mentioned in Surat al-Rahman are the categories, and *fi jannat* means "in these four gardens." These are categories, but their varieties are many.

As for the gardens, we explain them in the Shariah as the abodes of the righteous, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. So interpret the gardens of the Hereafter with this explanation: they are those which Allah prepared for the righteous, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

But when you read the saying of Allah the Exalted: **"Indeed, We tested them as We tested the people of the garden"** (68:17), how do you interpret *jannah* there? It means an orchard with many trees. When you read: **"Both gardens yielded their produce"** (18:33), you interpret it as an orchard with many trees. But do not interpret the Garden of Bliss in the Hereafter with this meaning. If you interpret it that way, the desire for it decreases and its greatness falls in people's hearts. Rather, say: it is the abode which Allah prepared for His friends, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Its inhabitants are the best of mankind: the Prophets, the *siddiqun* (the truthful, sincere believers), the martyrs, and the righteous. This is so that souls are stirred to act for it, and so that the ignorant person does not imagine that what is in it is like what is in this world.

As for His saying **"and rivers"**, it means the rivers. Allah the Exalted mentioned four categories of them in Surat Muhammad (Surah al-Qital). What are they?

* A student: **"The description of the Garden which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste never changes, and rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers, and rivers of purified honey"** (47:15).

* The Shaykh: Good. These are four categories. **"The description of the Garden which the righteous have been promised"**, meaning its description. **"In it are rivers"** is an explanation of the description. **"In it are rivers of water unaltered"**, meaning it never changes, neither by turbidity, nor by taste, nor by color, nor by smell. **"And rivers of milk whose taste never changes."** Milk in this world, when it is left, its taste changes, it spoils, and turns into an unbearable sourness. **"And rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers"**, and its delight is not like the delight of the wine of this world, and there is nothing in it of the defects of this world: **"They will not be affected by headache from it, nor will they be intoxicated"** (56:19). **"And rivers of purified honey"**, may Allah make us among those who drink from them: rivers of honey purified, with no beeswax in it, nor its harm, purified from every impurity.

This is an explanation of His saying: **"in gardens and rivers."** Then comes this place: **"in a seat of truth"** (54:55), meaning a seat in which there is no falsehood, neither in the report about it nor in its description. All of it is true. And in the presence of whom? **"In the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful"** (54:55), who is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may Allah make us among them. **"In the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful"**, they will enjoy the delight of looking at Allah the Mighty and Majestic, which is the greatest bliss for the people of Paradise. Allah the Exalted said: **"For those who did good is the best reward and more"** (10:26). *Al-husna* (the best reward) is Paradise, and *al-ziyadah* (the more) is looking at the Face of Allah. And He the Exalted said: **"Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord"** (75:22–23), meaning beautiful and bright. Allah clothes them with *nadr*, that is, goodness, beauty and splendor, so that they will be prepared to look at Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Then they look at Allah and their beauty increases above their beauty. For this reason, when they return to their families, their families will say to them: "You have become more beautiful after us," because of looking at the Face of Allah, blessed and exalted.

O Allah, we ask You by Your most beautiful names and Your highest attributes, that You make us among these people, by Your grace and generosity. Indeed You are over all things Competent.

* A student: **"The description of the Garden which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste never changes, and rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers, and rivers of purified honey"** (47:15).

* The Shaykh: Good. These are four categories. **"The description of the Garden which the righteous have been promised"**, meaning its description. **"In it are rivers"** is an explanation of the description. **"In it are rivers of water unaltered"**, meaning it never changes, neither by turbidity, nor by taste, nor by color, nor by smell. **"And rivers of milk whose taste never changes."** Milk in this world, when it is left, its taste changes, it spoils, and turns into an unbearable sourness. **"And rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers"**, and its delight is not like the delight of the wine of this world, and there is nothing in it of the defects of this world: **"They will not be affected by headache from it, nor will they be intoxicated"** (56:19). **"And rivers of purified honey"**, may Allah make us among those who drink from them: rivers of honey purified, with no beeswax in it, nor its harm, purified from every impurity.

This is an explanation of His saying: **"in gardens and rivers."** Then comes this place: **"in a seat of truth"** (54:55), meaning a seat in which there is no falsehood, neither in the report about it nor in its description. All of it is true. And in the presence of whom? **"In the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful"** (54:55), who is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may Allah make us among them. **"In the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful"**, they will enjoy the delight of looking at Allah the Mighty and Majestic, which is the greatest bliss for the people of Paradise. Allah the Exalted said: **"For those who did good is the best reward and more"** (10:26). *Al-husna* (the best reward) is Paradise, and *al-ziyadah* (the more) is looking at the Face of Allah. And He the Exalted said: **"Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord"** (75:22–23), meaning beautiful and bright. Allah clothes them with *nadr*, that is, goodness, beauty and splendor, so that they will be prepared to look at Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Then they look at Allah and their beauty increases above their beauty. For this reason, when they return to their families, their families will say to them: "You have become more beautiful after us," because of looking at the Face of Allah, blessed and exalted.

O Allah, we ask You by Your most beautiful names and Your highest attributes, that You make us among these people, by Your grace and generosity. Indeed You are over all things Competent.
